evidence.entities.table: RAM dump 2026-10-05 (Flycast via RetroArch READ_CORE_RAM, 16 KB requests): 0x8C477D40 = TObjPlayer, 20 TObjNpc*, 4 TObjCityDoor*, null-terminated
evidence.players_table: 0x8C42D92C holds the TObjPlayer pointer; the same address appears in the PSO V2 US CodeBreaker 'Unlimited HP' code
evidence.class: u32 at +0x00 points to the class-name string (same TObject layout as GameCube, little-endian)
evidence.entity_id/room: u16 +0x20: player 0, NPCs 0x1000.. consecutive; u16 +0x2C: room (player 0x29 in the Principal's office, NPCs 10/20 = same rooms as GameCube)
evidence.x/y/z: f32 +0x3C/+0x40/+0x44: player (0,0,-2015) at the office start and NPCs (179,0,342),(168,0,84),(156,0,-50), identical to the verified GameCube values
evidence.hp/tp: HUD HP 40/40 TP 29/29: u16 40/29 at +0x330/+0x332 (GameCube +0x32C shifted by the same 4 bytes as position) and +0x198/+0x19A. Which pair is current vs max: hypothesis until a damage test
evidence.angle: int32 at +0x64 tracks the movement heading (65536 = 360 deg): 275 vs 279 measured moving down, 236 vs 208 mid-turn (GameCube +0x60 shifted 4 bytes)

drop_tables.why: ItemRT.afs from the disc (40 raw tables). Each slot = probability byte + 3-byte item code; rate = (2 << max(0, ((p >> 3) & 31) - 4)) * ((p & 7) + 7) / 2^32 (newserv expand_rate). The game copies the tables into RAM; gBox finds those copies by content and rewrites the probability bytes.

camera.why: found 2026-10-06: float triples that follow the player (eye ~41 back / 26 up, target = player + ~20 up); projection checked on a paused frame (fence centre, Booma, player feet)
